claim_short: A documented longitudinal micro-EV model with battery, verified energy accounting and reproducible runs
scope_and_conditions: Documented model (docs/model.md, model_equations.md), not the thesis's own equations; energy closure <= 5.9e-10; dt convergence; Python-Modelica agreement for class A
recommended_action: Keep as a methodological contribution; describe as numerical verification not validation

claim_short: In the tested model, the thesis's SoH weight schedule gives no practical energy or tracking benefit over a fixed-gain LQR
scope_and_conditions: Documented model; thesis parameters (unverified); oracle SoH; S1, S2, UDDS, US06; SoH 1.0-0.7; 7 battery cases; ΔE -0.0019 % to +0.034 % in 112 pairs
recommended_action: Report as the primary finding with its scope

claim_short: A single retuned fixed gain matches or beats the SoH-scheduled controller (28 of 28 combinations)
scope_and_conditions: Same scope as A2; F01 selected once on S1 (prior study), out-of-sample elsewhere
recommended_action: Report

claim_short: Battery resistance growth alone raises energy use by about 0.16-1.1 % at SoH 0.7 and does not change tracking
scope_and_conditions: Thesis k_r0 = 0.5 (0.16-0.27 %) and sensitivity k_r0 = 2 (0.64-1.1 %) on S1/S2 at exact tracking; R1 class A range +0.17 % to +0.97 %
recommended_action: Report as the size of the ageing effect in this model

claim_short: On a fixed reference, a feedback gain can change energy only through the realised trajectory and the brake split; the best tested controller is within 0.11-0.20 % of exact tracking
scope_and_conditions: Class A plant; S1 and S2 (UDDS reference infeasible at 18 kW for 0.29 % of time); not a lower bound over trajectories with tracking tolerance
recommended_action: Report as the evaluation ceiling for any adaptive-gain energy claim on a fixed reference

claim_short: Each frozen-SoH LQR design is stable for the design model
scope_and_conditions: Discrete design model; frozen SoH; not a proof for time-varying SoH (audit M-11)
recommended_action: Keep; replace the thesis's time-varying Lyapunov proof (audit M-10/M-11)

claim_short: Battery ageing changes the controlled vehicle behaviour
scope_and_conditions: True only if battery current limits shrink with SoH (assumed BMS law, no source). Without it, ageing changes only I²R losses
recommended_action: State only with the condition; never as a property of the thesis cell

claim_short: 'Adaptive LQR with battery aging compensation' as the research direction
scope_and_conditions: Defensible as the tested hypothesis and design idea; not as an achieved compensation (none shown)
recommended_action: Keep the title; state in abstract/conclusion that compensation was hypothesised and tested, and not found in this model

claim_short: With equal tuning budgets, SoH scheduling gives no practical energy benefit over a fixed-gain LQR, with or without a battery-constraint supervisory layer, and there is no scheduling × supervision interaction
scope_and_conditions: Pre-registered P2 pilot (protocol SHA-256 ebebc157…2b5a); 257/257 valid runs; held-out S2 and UDDS; R0 ×1.1/×1.7; limits 3C/1C, 2C/0.5C, SoH-scaled (exploratory); |ΔE| ≤ 0.025 %, interaction ≤ 0.0033 pp; convergence change ≤ 4.2e-8 pp
recommended_action: Report as the confirmatory factorial test; label limits as assumed brackets

claim_short: A tuned fixed-gain LQR is an adequate baseline; SoH scheduling should be judged against an equally tuned fixed gain
scope_and_conditions: R1 budgets were unequal; the pilot used equal budgets, but its fixed search box excluded the most aggressive gains the scheduled family reached (post-hoc)
recommended_action: Adopt as the evaluation standard and state the search-box caveat

claim_short: The SoH-scheduled controller tracks better than the fixed controller in the aged condition
status: CONDITIONAL; not attributable to SoH information
scope_and_conditions: Pilot S2 SoH 0.8: RMSE 0.0173 vs 0.0234 m/s (ratio 0.741); reversed at SoH 1.0 (1.054); UDDS 0.990-1.002. Tracking is SoH-invariant to 3.4e-6 m/s where no drive limit binds, so the difference is a gain-magnitude effect a fixed gain can reproduce (analytical inference; not run)
recommended_action: Do not present as ageing compensation; at most 'a more aggressive gain improves tracking by ~0.006 m/s'

claim_short: A battery-constraint-aware supervisory layer (aware anti-windup + feasible-reference governor) improves behaviour under battery limits
scope_and_conditions: Inert where the drive limit does not bind; on UDDS ≤ 0.016 % energy, ≤ 3.3 % current-limit exceedance, ≤ 0.004 m/s overshoot; assumed limits
recommended_action: Do not claim a benefit; may be described as a design element that does no harm

claim_short: 12.5 % ± 2.1 % energy-efficiency improvement of adaptive over fixed-gain LQR
status: CONTRADICTED within the tested model and scenarios
scope_and_conditions: Documented model; S1, S2, UDDS, US06; oracle SoH; largest observed |ΔE| 0.034 %; not tested on NEDC/WLTP/CLTC/VUC or on a real vehicle
recommended_action: Remove; replace with the R1 result and its scope

claim_short: Ageing changes powertrain dynamics through ΔA(SoH) = ΔR_int/L_eq, which the adaptive gains compensate
scope_and_conditions: Battery resistance sits on the DC side of a current-controlled inverter; it does not enter speed/torque dynamics. L_eq and K_e have no values
recommended_action: Remove

claim_short: Reduced control authority due to increased internal resistance
scope_and_conditions: Voltage window binds only if R0 > 3.3-3.8 × new (k_r0 > 7.6-9.4 at SoH 0.7); never reached (V_t >= 42.97 V)
recommended_action: Remove or restate as a condition that would require much larger resistance growth

claim_short: Integral gain rises as SoH falls
scope_and_conditions: Gains computed from the documented design model fall; the thesis inputs (L_eq, K_e, K_t, γ) are missing
recommended_action: Replace with the computed schedule and its inputs

claim_short: The adaptive controller slows fade by moderating peak charge/discharge currents
status: CONTRADICTED as a mechanism in this model; contested in literature
scope_and_conditions: Peak current differs by <= 0.044 % between controllers (R1); Keil2015 found more regen generally reduced ageing; SunC2026: lower charging current alone does not establish a life benefit
recommended_action: Remove

claim_short: 15.3 % ± 2.8 % lower capacity fade over 1000 cycles
scope_and_conditions: No credible fade model; thesis model lacks constants and has inconsistent units; current or energy proxies are not fade evidence
recommended_action: Remove the number; state that fade was not evaluated; a fade claim needs a sourced cell, a fade law with uncertainty and an independent evaluation

claim_short: NSGA-II Pareto front for energy vs battery longevity
scope_and_conditions: Not reproduced (needs a fade model); Tawfik2024 already reports an NSGA-II degradation/charge-retention/driveability trade-off
recommended_action: Remove the results; if kept as method it must cite prior art and not claim novelty

claim_short: EKF/Coulomb-counting real-time SoH estimation accuracy
scope_and_conditions: Audit: the EKF as specified has no capacity state and cannot identify capacity; no estimator was implemented in R1 (oracle SoH)
recommended_action: Remove accuracy figures; describe the estimator as future work

claim_short: Results on NEDC, WLTP, CLTC, VUC and against PID, fuzzy LQR, MPC, DDPG
scope_and_conditions: No reproducible implementation of these cycles/benchmarks in the project
recommended_action: Remove or label as not reproduced

claim_short: Novelty of an SoH-scheduled LQR framework
scope_and_conditions: Not found by OpenAlex/Crossref/web search; IEEE Xplore and Scopus not searched; Pan2023 and Tawfik2024 overlap neighbouring claims
recommended_action: Do not claim novelty or 'first'

claim_short: Parameters validated against datasheets and published data
scope_and_conditions: 20 of 39 parameters are thesis values without primary source; the cell is unidentified (16 × 3.2 V ≠ 48 V)
recommended_action: Relabel as assumed/unverified; supply the cell part number (OC-1)

claim_short: For an identified 48 V LFP micro-EV cell with datasheet state-of-power limits, SoH-dependent power capability changes achievable tracking on urban cycles
scope_and_conditions: Literature: small packs become power-limited before capacity-limited (Etxandi2024, NMC+LMO); retailer 100 Ah LFP ratings (1C continuous, 2C pulse; SEC) imply a battery-limited regime for an 18 kW motor
recommended_action: Separate R2 only after OC-1 is resolved; affects both controllers alike unless a controller uses the limit information

claim_short: Scheduling the LQR on available power (state of power) rather than on SoH changes behaviour under binding limits
scope_and_conditions: Komaee2024 (gain adapted to avoid saturation); pilot shows both branches sit on the same limit when it binds
recommended_action: Only with sourced limits; pre-register against an equally tuned fixed gain + anti-windup

claim_short: An energy-time-health Pareto frontier for a micro-EV with LQR inner loop, at equal trip time or across a declared time budget
scope_and_conditions: Lot2025, LiB2024, Tawfik2024, Cai2026 cover the line; ledger shows 5 % slower → 4.1-5.4 % less energy per km
recommended_action: Separate study with its own gap check; never reported as an LQR or SoH-scheduling gain

claim_short: A capacity-fade comparison between controllers using a sourced LFP fade law (e.g. Naumann2020 or Wang2011) with parameter uncertainty
scope_and_conditions: Stress indicators differ by ≤ 0.23 % (Ah), ≤ 0.044 % (peak current) between controllers; Keil2015 warns lower peak current need not reduce fade
recommended_action: Only with a fade law for an identified cell; expect a null within the law's uncertainty

claim_short: A benchmark protocol for adaptive EV controller claims: equal tuning budgets, gap-to-exact-tracking bound, energy ledger, completion guard, cross-simulator check
status: OPEN; supported by this project's tooling
scope_and_conditions: Mahdy2026 (> 73 % simulation-only; reproducibility weak); Hattori2020 (standard cycles cannot evaluate trajectory-changing methods)
recommended_action: Viable as a methods paper or thesis chapter framed as evaluation methodology
